name: cloakbrowser
description: CloakBrowser stealth Chromium through the Playwright MCP tool contract, via cloakbrowser-mcp. Its camoufox engine runs through a plugin-owned overlay that restores the stock search engines (Google by default).

headless.title: Headless
headless.description: Run the browser without a window. Headed mode is measurably less detectable, so leave this off unless you need a server with no display.

browser_engine.title: Browser engine
browser_engine.description: cloak uses the patched CloakBrowser Chromium. playwright uses the stock Playwright Chromium and gives up the stealth patches. camoufox uses the Camoufox stealth Firefox and needs Python 3.12+ with uv installed. camoufox-native uses the user-installed mcp-camoufox package (its own 27-tool contract, portable by default; install it yourself, the plugin does not bundle it). kameleo attaches to a running Kameleo Chroma profile over CDP and needs the Kameleo app with an active licence and a profile ID; Junglefox profiles cannot be attached, and stealth over attach is unverified. The engine is read when the MCP server starts; changing it restarts the server and reloads the tool list.

tool_profile.title: Tool profile
tool_profile.description: Which tools the selected engine exposes. default follows the engine manifest: full for cloak and playwright (the current 77-tool surface); portable for camoufox, camoufox-native and kameleo (a shared 24-tool core). portable hides engine-specific and extra tools; full exposes everything the engine supports. The seven tool groups and disabled_tools still apply. Restart Claude Code after changing it.

camoufox_profile.title: Camoufox native profile
camoufox_profile.description: Profile name for the camoufox-native engine. One name per account. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only, starting with a letter or digit, up to 64 characters. Cookies and logins are kept under this name; a second Claude Code session using the same name is refused by the engine.

camoufox_data_dir.title: Camoufox native data directory
camoufox_data_dir.description: Where the camoufox-native engine keeps its profiles and logs. Leave empty for Claude Code's plugin data directory (profiles/camoufox-native). Each profile is a 'profiles/<name>' folder inside it. Use one directory per set of accounts.

kameleo_profile_id.title: Kameleo profile ID
kameleo_profile_id.description: Profile ID to attach to. Required when the browser engine is kameleo. Open Kameleo, create or start the profile, and copy its ID from the profile row. The plugin never starts the Kameleo app; it connects to Kameleo's local API, which starts the profile. Chromium (Chroma) profiles only: a Junglefox profile cannot be attached over CDP.

kameleo_endpoint.title: Kameleo CDP endpoint (optional)
kameleo_endpoint.description: Full WebSocket CDP endpoint for the Kameleo profile. Leave empty to use ws://127.0.0.1:5050/playwright/<profile ID>. Only ws:// or wss:// on a loopback host is accepted; a non-loopback endpoint is rejected.

tools_vision.title: Mouse primitives (vision)
tools_vision.description: Six coordinate mouse tools: click, move, drag, down, up and wheel. Off removes them.

tools_devtools.title: Tracing, video and highlights
tools_devtools.description: Thirteen devtools tools: tracing, video, recording, annotations and element highlights. Off removes them.

tools_storage.title: Cookies and web storage
tools_storage.description: Seventeen storage tools: cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and storage state. Off removes them.

tools_network.title: Network routing
tools_network.description: Four network tools: route, unroute, route list and network state. Off removes request interception.

tools_testing.title: Assertions and locator generation
tools_testing.description: Five testing tools: generate_locator and the four verify_* assertions. Off removes them.

tools_config.title: Configuration read
tools_config.description: browser_get_config. Off removes the configuration introspection tool.

disabled_tools.title: Disabled tools
disabled_tools.description: Comma-separated tool names to hide from the agent and reject when called, for example browser_pdf_save,browser_start_video. Leave empty to expose the selected profile unchanged.

humanize.title: Humanised input
humanize.description: Human-like mouse paths, keystroke timing and scrolling instead of instant synthetic events.

human_preset.title: Humanised input preset
human_preset.description: default is the normal humanised behaviour. careful is slower and more deliberate.

release_channel.title: Engine release channel
release_channel.description: stable is the free channel. preview requires a CloakBrowser Pro licence.

geoip_proxy_match.title: Match timezone and locale to the proxy
geoip_proxy_match.description: Resolve the proxy exit location and align the browser timezone and locale to it. Enable this together with a proxy server.

profile_isolation.title: Profile isolation
profile_isolation.description: Session safety for the browser profile. shared keeps one profile per account for every Claude Code window, exactly as before. workspace gives each project folder its own profile (profiles/<engine>/ws-<hash>) so two projects do not collide; that profile starts with a fresh login state, and if it is already in use the plugin uses a numbered sibling (ws-<hash>-2 to -5) and reports the switch. isolated uses no browser profile at all: no profile directory is created or locked, cookies, logins and storage are not saved, and nothing persists after the session; Profile directory, Account profile and the default-profile pointer are ignored and reported for that start, and several sessions can run at once. copy runs the session on a temporary copy of the profile that Profile directory, Account profile, the default-profile pointer or the engine default resolves: the base profile is locked for the session and never written, the browser starts on the copy, and the copy is discarded when the session ends cleanly; a crashed session leaves it under profiles/<engine>/.sessions, where browser_profiles list shows it and scripts/profile-copy.mjs --prune removes it. copy-keep does the same and keeps the changes: when the session ends cleanly the base profile is replaced by the session copy and the old base is retained beside it as <name>.previous-<timestamp>; those retained trees are never deleted automatically and accumulate until you remove them. A crash or a hard kill performs no swap: the base stays untouched and the session copy is kept. copy-keep is refused when the base is outside the plugin data directory. copy does not combine with workspace in this version, and neither does copy-keep. In shared, workspace, copy and copy-keep, Profile directory and Account profile win over the mode. The free CloakBrowser tier still allows one browser at a time. Restart Claude Code after changing it.

on_locked.title: When the profile is in use
on_locked.description: What this session does when the browser profile it resolved is already in use by another process. block stops the backend and exposes only the broker meta-tools until Claude Code restarts the MCP server. fallback, the default, starts on the first free numbered sibling of the profile (profiles/.../<name>-2 to -5) and reports the switch everywhere: that profile has separate cookies, logins and fingerprint seed, and it is never the profile the other session is using; when -2 to -5 are all in use, no backend starts and the message names the owner. isolated starts with no profile at all: nothing is saved and nothing persists. Only profiles the plugin manages are given siblings or an isolated start; an explicit Profile directory is never duplicated and keeps the block behaviour. It applies to shared, workspace, pointer and account profiles and to the copy modes, where the sibling becomes the copy base; it has no effect on camoufox-native or kameleo, which manage their own profiles. Restart Claude Code after changing it.

identity_mode.title: Device identity (Camoufox)
identity_mode.description: How the Camoufox engine presents its device identity. profile gives each persistent Camoufox profile one generated identity: the first launch draws a fingerprint for this computer's operating system, stores it in <profile>/.camoufox-identity.json and reuses it on every later launch, so a site that keeps cookies also sees the same device (Camoufox otherwise draws a new one on every launch). Delete that file to draw a new identity on the next start; a copied profile carries it, so delete it inside the copy to give the copy a different device. random restores the per-launch draw. An isolated start has no profile to store anything in, so it always draws a new identity. This setting is inert for the other engines: cloak pins its own Chromium seed, playwright and camoufox-native have no fingerprint input, and Kameleo manages its own profiles; browser_capabilities says so and reports the active source, the identity file and when it was created.

ping_timeout_ms.title: Server heartbeat timeout (Camoufox)
ping_timeout_ms.description: Applies to the camoufox engine only: how long its backend waits for an answer to its own heartbeat ping before it closes the browser and ends the session, in milliseconds. 0 is the default and disables the wrapper's heartbeat entirely. The backend pings every 3 s and closes the browser when an answer is more than 5 s late; one late answer (a stalled Claude Code event loop, a busy machine, sleep or resume) was enough to lose the browser, and a dead client is still detected through the MCP pipe itself. A positive value re-enables the heartbeat with that deadline, so a client that does not answer within it still loses the browser and the session. A non-negative integer; anything else is ignored with one log line and the heartbeat stays disabled. The other engines send no server heartbeat and ignore this setting, and browser_capabilities and browser_engine_status say so. An explicit PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS in the environment wins over this setting.

password_manager.title: Saved logins and autofill (Camoufox)
password_manager.description: Off by default. When on, Camoufox's Firefox password manager is enabled for this profile: saved logins in the profile's logins.db can be autofilled into matching login forms, and Firefox will offer to save new logins. This is a deliberate security trade-off. Autofilled credentials can be read by the page's own scripts, by the model through browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate, and by a prompt-injected page that steers the model to a login form; the plugin cannot tell a legitimate login page from a phishing one. The store is encrypted with the profile's key4.db, which sits in the same profile and is not bound to your Windows account (no primary password is set by default): anyone who obtains the profile (a copy, a backup, profile_isolation=copy or copy-keep, or scripts/profile-copy.mjs) can decrypt the saved passwords. Autofill on plain HTTP stays off, and address/credit-card autofill and form history stay off. The pinned Camoufox build disables the manager by enterprise policy (PasswordManagerEnabled: false, OfferToSaveLogins: false), and launch prefs alone lose to that lock. The camoufox engine always runs on a plugin-owned overlay of that build inside the plugin data directory (hardlinks and junctions to the build; only distribution/policies.json is replaced, every other policy preserved; about 0 bytes on a normal install, about 310 MB only when the build cache is on another volume). The overlay restores the stock search engines with Google as the default on every start; turning this setting on adds the two password policies and the three signon prefs to that same overlay, and turning it off removes only those. It is verified once with a short headless start, and browser_capabilities reports the overlay directory, its mode and the policy path. If the overlay cannot be created or verified, the stock build runs normally and browser_capabilities reports blocked-by-overlay with the reason; a directory this plugin did not write is never touched and reports blocked-by-existing-overlay. Inert for cloak, playwright and kameleo; camoufox-native has no prefs input and reports native-unavailable. The plugin never reads, logs or transmits logins.db or key4.db, and this setting never authorizes typing, submitting, recovering or handling 2FA or CAPTCHA on a credential form.

account.title: Account profile
account.description: Browser profile name for one account. Each name keeps its own cookies, logins and fingerprint seed under Claude Code's plugin data directory (profiles/<engine>/<name>). Leave empty to use the plugin's default profile (profiles/default). Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only, starting with a letter or digit, up to 64 characters, no trailing dot or space. Ignored when Persistent profile directory is set. Changing it takes effect when the Claude Code MCP server restarts; sign in to each account manually in the headed window.

profile_dir.title: Persistent profile directory
profile_dir.description: Directory that keeps cookies, logins and the fingerprint seed. It is created if it does not exist. Leave empty to use the plugin's own persistent profile in Claude Code's plugin data directory (profiles/default). Use one directory per account.

proxy_server.title: Proxy server
proxy_server.description: Sticky proxy URL, for example http://user:pass@host:port. Leave empty for a direct connection.

proxy_bypass.title: Proxy bypass list
proxy_bypass.description: Comma-separated hosts that should not use the proxy. Leave empty to proxy everything.

licence_key.title: CloakBrowser licence key
licence_key.description: CloakBrowser Pro key. The free tier works without it and allows one concurrent session. Stored in the operating system credential store.

engine_version.title: Engine version pin
engine_version.description: Pin a specific CloakBrowser Chromium build. Leave empty to use the stable channel and let the binary update itself.

output_dir.title: Artifacts directory
output_dir.description: Where Playwright MCP writes screenshots, traces and session files. It is created if it does not exist. Leave empty to write them to .playwright-mcp in the folder the client opened (its first file root), or, when the client advertises no usable file root, to the plugin data folder under output/<engine>.

allow_unrestricted_file_access.title: Unrestricted file access
allow_unrestricted_file_access.description: Remove Playwright's file-access allowlist for tool-chosen paths and unblock file:// navigation, so the model can read and write any file your operating-system user can, not only the Artifacts directory and the workspace root. A deliberate security trade-off: a prompt-injected page could make the model read or overwrite private files. Leave this off unless you need a path outside those roots. Applies to the cloak, playwright, camoufox and kameleo engines; the camoufox-native engine has no file-path tools and ignores it.

extension_paths.title: Unpacked extensions
extension_paths.description: Absolute directories of unpacked Chromium extensions to load in every start, as a JSON string array or a comma-separated list. Unpacked directories only: the Chrome Web Store is not available in this Chromium, and a directory cannot contain a comma. Any and all extensions you list are allowed. An extension is privileged code that runs with the browser's privileges on every page and is outside the MCP tool filters: it bypasses disabled_tools, can read page content, cookies and storage, and can send that anywhere your network allows, so only load directories you trust. There is no signature check at load and no automatic update. Its stored data lives in the browser profile and therefore travels with profile copies, retained previous trees and backups. Applies to the cloak engine only, which must run on a persistent profile: with profile_isolation isolated (or on_locked isolated) the server refuses to start until the extension list is cleared or a persistent profile mode is chosen. While the list is set, only these directories are enabled, and any extension you installed by hand in the profile stays disabled for that start. In shared, workspace and account profiles the extension state persists; profile_isolation copy discards a session's extension changes when it ends cleanly, and copy-keep keeps them by swapping the session copy into the base. The other engines ignore the setting and say so in browser_capabilities. An explicit CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_PATHS in the environment wins over this setting.
